key_insight: Increasing the per-frame token budget and managing those tokens with a dynamic key-value (KV) cache lets streaming models retain fine-grained spatiotemporal details, improving retrieval and question answering over long video streams without treating memory as a fixed low-resolution summary.
problem_solved: Streaming video understanding and VQA suffer when per-frame representations are compressed into too few tokens, losing fine-grained visual detail and temporal context; this work addresses how to scale and manage token memory so models can store and retrieve richer frame information over time.
method: Scale per-frame tokenization to produce more spatially and temporally granular tokens, then write those tokens into a KV-cache rather than discarding details.
Introduce dynamic KV-cache memory management (importance-based allocation, eviction, and aggregation) so the cache grows/contracts with stream demands while controlling compute and latency.
Efficient retrieval for question answering via selective attention/lookup over the cached keys and values, enabling the model to combine long-range context with high-resolution frame detail.
impact: Provides a practical recipe for building streaming video models that keep richer history without catastrophic memory bloat—improving accuracy on long-horizon VQA and other continuous-vision tasks while offering controllable trade-offs between fidelity, latency, and memory.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: live video frames → dense tokenization → dynamic KV-cache (write/evict) → query/retrieve → VQA output
Before/After comparison: low-token per-frame (blurry/aggregated) vs. scaled-token per-frame (fine-grained spatial detail) illustrations
Performance chart: accuracy vs. token budget and memory usage (showing gains as tokens scale with dynamic caching)
Timeline/memory visualization: video stream with highlighted important tokens kept, less-relevant tokens evicted, and retrieval arrows to show query readout
paper_title: Going Down Memory Lane: Scaling Tokens for Video Stream Understanding with Dynamic KV-Cache Memory
paper_authors: Vatsal Agarwal, Saksham Suri, Matthew Gwilliam, Pulkit Kumar, Abhinav Shrivastava
